answers.question: Who are the pre-processors within about 150 km of Bengaluru that turn yard bales and lots into factory feedstock (PET flake/washing lines, plastic reprocessors, cable granulators, tyre shredders/crumb/pyrolysis, C&D plants, ELV/RVSFs, e-waste dismantlers, used-oil re-refiners, foundry-sand reclaimers)? Give counts, names, capacities and clusters.
answers.answer: Plastics (Orange 1326/1366): CPCB's Karnataka plastic-recycler list (as on 01-03-2022) names units and capacities, e.g. Keerthana Enterprises Unit-2, Peenya (1,320 MT/yr), Anwar Enterprises, Yeshwanthpura (600 MT/yr), RNZ Recycling, Kumbalagodu (1,560 MT/yr), Prem Industries, Peenya, and Ishvarya Traders, Jigani (3,000 MT/yr); a CPCB status snippet puts Karnataka at 143 recycling units with 2.10 lakh tonnes/yr capacity, and the 2020-21 CPCB annual report counted 239 plastic manufacturing/recycling units plus 128 unregistered ones, so a current count must come from the CPCB EPR plastic portal PWP list, which could not be opened. No named PET hot-wash flake line near Bengaluru was confirmed from any snippet; Bengaluru listings show PET-flake traders and washing-line machinery vendors (R Mech Machines sells lines into Karnataka), so PET-flake capacity within 150 km is an open item. E-waste (Red 1120): KSPCB has authorised 27 collection centres, 42 dismantlers, 24 recyclers and 14 recycler-cum-dismantlers (Deccan Herald, undated snippet); named units are E-Parisaraa (Dobaspet KIADB, about 50 km out on the Tumkur road, India's first authorised recycler), Ash Recyclers, Thimmaiah Road (52,722 MT/yr on a CPCB list), Cerebra Integrated Technologies (up to 90,000 t/yr), Eco-E-Waste Recyclers and Nobel Technology (300 MT/yr each on the older list), plus Attero/Ecobirdd collection presence. Tyres (Orange 1424): a Quint report says Karnataka had 34 tyre-pyrolysis units, of which 12 complied with the CPCB SOP, 3 shut and 19 were non-compliant, and KSPCB issued closure orders to 8; the CPCB waste-tyre EPR portal (eprtyres.cpcb.gov.in) holds the current recycler list by state but no Karnataka-specific names or crumb-rubber capacities appeared in snippets. C&D (Orange 1414): Bengaluru generates 2,000-2,500 t/day; Rock Crystals at Chikkajala is rated 1,000 TPD but ran at about 10% (around 200 t/day) for lack of demand, the Kannur plant is 750 TPD, a Jigani unit also receives debris, the two BBMP plants get only 100-200 t/day, and Chaitra Civil Ventures won a Rs 1,052-crore, 15-year contract to feed 1,750 t/day to Kannur and Chikkajala (Deccan Herald, undated snippet). ELV (Orange 1405): Karnataka's first RVSF is Mahindra MSTC Recycling (CERO) at Sy. No. 67, Haradiapura, Vijayapura/Devanahalli, Bengaluru Rural 562135, about 25,000 vehicles/yr with room to expand; Koratagere and Koppal RVSFs were announced but their status could not be confirmed. Used oil: the MoEF/CPCB registered re-refiner list includes Lube Tech Petrochemicals, Veerasandra (1,440 KL/yr), Balaji Refineries, Veerasandra (1,100 KL/yr), Arun Industries, Peenya 3rd Stage (360 KL/yr), Nakoda Petrochemical, Tumkur, and Century Refineries at Hoskote holds KSPCB consent and CPCB registration. Lead-acid batteries (a CPCB list, 672 units nationally, 32 in Karnataka with 419,056 MTA): Sri Ponni Industries, Bommasandra (5,000 MTA), Veera Narayana Metal Industries, Magadi taluk (36,000 MTA), Evershine Smelting, Attibele (3,200 MTA), Sri Saraswathi Industries, Veerasandra (3,200 MTA), Mekala Metal Works (3,000 MTA). Cable granulation and foundry-sand reclamation are mostly in-house or trader-run (Urban Eco Recyclers advertises automated cable granulation in Bengaluru; Belgaum Foundry Cluster runs a 10-tonne green-sand reclamation plant, but Belagavi is about 500 km away), so no standalone Bengaluru cable-granulator or sand-reclaimer count exists. Clusters confirmed by addresses: Peenya (plastics, used oil), Bommasandra-Attibele-Veerasandra-Jigani (batteries, used oil, plastics), Dobaspet/Nelamangala-Tumkur road (e-waste, hazardous-waste zone), Kumbalagodu-Kengeri (plastics), Devanahalli-Chikkajala-Kannur-Bagalur (ELV, C&D), Hoskote (used oil).
answers.decision: Seed the pre-processor role with the named units above (about 20) and treat capacity as a self-declared field; before the pilot, pull the CPCB EPR plastic-portal PWP list for Karnataka and the KSPCB e-waste list to fill the counts, and prioritise Peenya and Bommasandra-Jigani for onboarding since both have plastics, battery and oil processors within one trip of the south and north yards.
answers.whoToAsk: KSPCB regional offices (Peenya and Bommasandra) for the XGN consent register by category code; the CPCB EPR plastic and tyre portals for the current Karnataka PWP and tyre-recycler lists; BBMP SWM for the Kannur and Jigani operator names; a phone call to E-Parisaraa, Rock Crystals and Mahindra CERO for live capacities.

answers.question: What do these pre-processors pay yards for bales and lots, what do they sell outputs for, and what lot sizes, payment terms, freight, quality deductions and sourcing rules apply?
answers.answer: Buy-side (L3, what a pre-processor pays a yard), from marketplace listings only, none Bengaluru-specific unless stated: PET bottle bales Rs 22-35/kg clear and Rs 15-25/kg mixed colour (Chennai bale listing Rs 29/kg; a Rs 30-35/kg minimum for natural bales), HDPE baled scrap about Rs 48/kg (a Challakere, Karnataka listing) with graded HDPE up to Rs 75-100/kg, LDPE film scrap Rs 40-75/kg (post-industrial bales Rs 65/kg), OCC Rs 12-16/kg baled to traders and Rs 14-18/kg mill-grade delivered to mills, HMS in Bengaluru Rs 28-55/kg across listings (Karnataka range Rs 36-49/kg; a July 2026 Bengaluru quote of Rs 55/kg), baled clean UBC Rs 95-120/kg (Delhi quotes Rs 194-238/kg on 29 Jan 2026 show how wide this swings), whole scrap tyres Rs 12-22/kg (Hyderabad Rs 12, Ahmedabad Rs 13, Delhi Rs 20), insulated copper cable Rs 340-520/kg (Delhi Rs 415/kg, Sep 2026). No India price for intact lead-acid batteries per kg was found in any snippet; it is an open item. Sell-side (L3/L4 outputs): hot-washed PET flakes Rs 55-65/kg typical with listings up to Rs 82/kg, cold-washed flakes about Rs 52/kg, rPET granules Rs 75-90/kg (and India rPET flake index USD 763/t in Q2 2026), reprocessed HDPE granules Rs 65-77/kg (R-HDPE index USD 1,238/t, June 2026), recycled PP granules Rs 55-82/kg, millberry/bare-bright copper Rs 680-800/kg (copper granules were not quoted separately; assume a small discount to millberry), crumb rubber Rs 22-35/kg, tyre pyrolysis oil Rs 25-50/litre (typical Rs 28-32), recycled aggregate from C&D about Rs 350-400/tonne against Rs 630-770/tonne crushed stone and Rs 1,250/tonne M-sand in Bengaluru (Aug 2026); Rock Crystals historically charged a Rs 134/tonne tipping fee including GST. No snippet gave LDPE agglomerate or shredded-steel prices, so both are open items. Terms: no Indian pre-processor publishes lot sizes, credit terms, freight or deduction rules; the only documented rules are the APR/ISRI model bale specs (truckload of roughly 16 t, moisture over 4% deducted at tested-percent minus 2%, no single contaminant above 2%), which Indian buyers apply informally as visual grading and a weight cut on delivery. Sourcing: Hasiru Dala Innovations states it aggregates PET from waste-picker entrepreneurs, dry-waste collection centres and scrap dealers, and the PET-flake trade in Bengaluru runs through traders, so pre-processors mostly buy from yards, traders and aggregators rather than from individual kabadiwalas; a DWCC with a baler can sell direct only if it can fill a truck.
answers.decision: Set L3 reference prices in the pilot from these ranges (PET bale Rs 25-32/kg, HDPE bale Rs 45-50/kg, OCC Rs 12-16/kg, HMS Rs 36-45/kg, UBC Rs 100-120/kg, tyres Rs 12-18/kg, cable Rs 350-450/kg) as editable defaults, record every lot with a moisture and contamination percentage and a buyer deduction field, default freight to buyer-arranged pickup for a minimum lot of one full truck (about 8-16 tonnes baled) and cash or UPI on weighbridge weight, and confirm all of it with ten phone quotes in Peenya and Bommasandra during the first fortnight.
answers.whoToAsk: Ten pre-processors (three plastics reprocessors in Peenya and Jigani, one PET flake buyer, one e-waste dismantler at Dobaspet, one battery smelter in Bommasandra, one used-oil re-refiner at Veerasandra or Hoskote, Rock Crystals, one tyre crumb unit, one cable granulator) for current buy and sell prices, minimum lots, credit days and deduction rules; Hasiru Dala Innovations and Saahas for what DWCCs actually receive for baled PET; a CA for GST and TCS treatment on the recorded prices.
